rows.note: Use this as the all-purpose way to describe something physically higher, such as the upper shelf or upper floor.

example.english: There’s a cha chaan teng on the upper floor.
example.traditional: 上面嗰層樓有間茶餐廳。
example.jyutping: soeng6 min6 go2 cang4 lau4 jau5 gaan1 caa4 caan1 teng1

rows.note: Use this when “upper” means higher-ranking or higher-level, rather than for physical position.

example.english: This is a restaurant at the upper end of the market, and we can’t afford it.
example.traditional: 呢間係高級餐廳，我哋食唔起㗎。
example.jyutping: ni1 gaan1 hai6 gou1 kap1 caan1 teng1 ngo5 dei6 sik6 m4 hei2 gaa3

rows.note: Use this for something situated upstream or in the upper reaches of a river.

example.english: The water quality in the upper reaches is better.
example.jyutping: soeng6 jau4 ge3 seoi2 zat1 hou2 di1

rows.note: Use this attributive construction for anything pertaining to secondary school.

example.english: Students in the upper school have to wear uniforms.
example.jyutping: zung1 hok6 ge3 hok6 saang1 jiu3 zoek3 haau6 fuk6
